answer: Each agent can submit only one claim per fixed period, and a claim counts only after a randomly selected peer has verified it against a signed, publicly auditable record. Verification peers are drawn from identities with prior accepted claims, so a new identity cannot immediately vouch for its own swarm. An attacker must therefore build history and spend real verification effort for every extra identity, slowing a sybil spiral. The timber ledger may track ivory deliveries, but those words alone grant no trust.
